messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Hospital Course:

The patient was admitted with cough, weight loss, and a cavity in the right upper pulmonary lobe. The patient tested positive for HIV and was diagnosed with tuberculosis infection. After starting antiviral and anti-tuberculosis therapy, the patient presented with urinary retention due to an enlarged prostate. The patient was transferred to a tertiary care hospital for further management.

Assessment and Plan:

During the hospital stay, the patient underwent several diagnostic tests including sputum culture, smear, and interferon-γ release assay, which were negative for Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Lumbar puncture indicated nearly normal cerebrospinal fluid profile, and CT scan revealed a cavity with effusion in the upper right lung. Bronchoscopy confirmed the presence of Cryptococcus neoformans in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Enhanced MRI of the prostate showed an abnormal patchy signal in the central gland of the prostate with reduced T2W1 signal in the seminal vesicles and peripheral zone of the prostate. A prostatic biopsy revealed granulomatous inflammation with positive periodic acid–Schiff staining. Culture of the prostatic tissue grew Cryptococcus neoformans.

The patient was diagnosed with AIDS with pulmonary cryptococcosis and cryptococcal prostatitis. Oral voriconazole and flucytosine combination therapy for 2 months followed by oral fluconazole maintenance treatment for 4 months was initiated and relieved the patient’s urinary retention and the cryptococcal prostatitis.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Plan:

The patient was discharged in stable condition with a prescription for oral fluconazole. The patient was advised to follow up with an infectious disease specialist for further management of the underlying condition of AIDS. The patient was also advised to take necessary precautions to prevent future infections.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for this admission is AIDS presenting with disseminated cryptococcosis, involving the lung and the prostate. The cough, cavity and urinary retention were symptoms of that infection, so they are not the principal diagnosis. This falls in chapter B, and under Australian Coding Standard 0102 the HIV disease is sequenced first. My recollection, which I have not verified, is that ICD-10-AM uses the single category B24 rather than B20.

CODE: B24
